standard_prerequisites.name: The interval as a higher inductive type
standard_prerequisites.statement: The interval is generated by two points and a path between them, so a map out of it is given by two points and a path between their images.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the structure the proof has to respect.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dependent action on paths
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a dependent function f a path s in the base gives a dependent path from f of one endpoint to f of the other, which must be supplied to define f on the path constructor.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the datum the proof constructs by hand.

standard_prerequisites.name: Path inverses are inverses
standard_prerequisites.statement: For any path its inverse concatenated with it is equal to reflexivity.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the canonical element that closes the construction.

core_obligations: Show that every point of the interval is equal to one of its endpoints, by defining a function into the path type from that endpoint (source lines 389-391).
Give the values of that function at the two point constructors, with the required path types (source lines 391-395).

Determine the dependent action on paths at the interval path constructor, whose type reduces by computation to the statement that the inverse of the path concatenated with it is reflexivity (source lines 396-398).
Supply that canonical element, which completes the function and hence the contractibility (source line 398).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the contraction function on the two points.
Compute the datum required on the path constructor and supply it from the inverse law.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 384-386: the interval is contractible. The statement says nothing about how the contraction is produced, and the proof (source lines 388-398) has to define a dependent function out of a higher inductive type, which means giving not only its values at the two point constructors but also the dependent path required at the interval constructor; the manuscript computes that type explicitly, reduces it to the assertion that the inverse of the interval path concatenated with it is reflexivity, and closes the argument with the canonical proof of the inverse law. The whole content is the bookkeeping of the dependent action on paths at a path constructor, and none of it is visible in the statement.
